record.paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
record.original_question: For a Riemannian n-manifold M, what Riemannian conditions obstruct the existence of an isometric Lagrangian immersion M -> C^n? Here C^n is complex Euclidean n-space, and a Lagrangian submanifold is a totally real submanifold whose real dimension equals the complex dimension of the ambient Kahler manifold, equivalently the totally real case with the smallest possible codimension.

evidence.quote: A totally real submanifold M of a Kahler manifold M~ is known as a Lagrangian submanifold if dim_R M = dim_C M~; in other word, a Lagrangian submanifold is a totally real submanifold with the smallest possible codimension.
Problem 3.1. What are Riemannian obstructions to Lagrangian isometric immersions of a Riemannian n-manifold into C^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian $n$-manifold, and let $\mathbb{C}^n$ denote complex Euclidean $n$-space endowed with its standard flat Kähler structure (Euclidean metric, standard complex structure $J$, and Kähler form $\omega$). An isometric immersion $f:M\to \mathbb{C}^n$ is called Lagrangian if $f^*\omega=0$; equivalently, $J(df(T_pM))$ is the normal space of $f(M)$ at each $p\in M$, so $f(M)$ is a totally real submanifold whose real dimension equals the complex dimension of the ambient Kähler manifold (the smallest possible codimension for a totally real submanifold). Determine intrinsic Riemannian conditions on $(M,g)$ — formulated purely in terms of curvature invariants (e.g. sectional, Ricci, scalar curvature, or other Riemannian invariants of $g$) — that obstruct the existence of any isometric Lagrangian immersion $f:M\to \mathbb{C}^n$. In particular, find nontrivial necessary conditions that $(M,g)$ must satisfy in order to admit such an immersion.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a broad research program rather than a single yes/no question. Substantial partial results are known: B.-Y. Chen and collaborators have produced numerous Riemannian obstructions to Lagrangian isometric immersions in $\mathbb{C}^n$ (and more generally complex space forms) via the δ-invariants (Chen invariants) and associated optimal inequalities, beginning with "Some new obstructions to minimal and Lagrangian isometric immersions" (2000) and continuing through work on ideal Lagrangian immersions. However, a complete intrinsic characterization of Riemannian $n$-manifolds admitting an isometric Lagrangian immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$ is not known, so the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Some new obstructions to minimal and Lagrangian isometric immersions
status_evidence.snippet: New Riemannian invariants (δ-invariants) yielding obstructions to minimal and Lagrangian isometric immersions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial obstructions via δ-invariants have been established.

status_evidence.title: Ideal Lagrangian immersions in complex space forms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ideal Lagrangian immersions and corresponding inequalities in complex space forms.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines obstructions and characterizes equality cases.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (arXiv:1307.1875)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing immersibility problems and δ-invariant obstructions for Lagrangian immersions.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates this is an ongoing research program with partial answers.
